title: He was chosen…
paragraphs:
He was chosen…
before the goodbye.

Before the grief had time to settle.
Before the shadow of a giant stepped aside.
Before the fear even had a name.

And if you’re honest—
that’s exactly what scares you.
Because you thought God would wait.

Wait until you’re healed.
Wait until you’re confident.
Wait until the person you leaned on is no longer in the picture.

But He didn’t wait for Joshua.
And He’s not waiting for you.
In , the moment is raw—Moses is still alive, still present, still towering… and yet God calls Joshua forward anyway. Not after the loss. Not after closure.
Right in the middle of it.

That tension you feel?
That in-between place where something hasn’t fully ended, but something new is already demanding your obedience?
That’s not confusion.
That’s calling.
Joshua stood there with dust on his skin and doubt in his chest.

He wasn’t Moses.
He didn’t carry the same history.
He didn’t have the same voice, the same encounters, the same burning bush.
And deep down, there’s a question we rarely admit:
“What if I’m not enough for what God is asking?”
So we delay.

We obey halfway.
We hide behind preparation.
We spiritualize our hesitation and call it “waiting on God.”
But some of you aren’t waiting on God.
God is waiting on you.
Let it cut.
Because delayed obedience is still disobedience.

And quiet compromise doesn’t make you safe—
it makes you stuck.

Joshua could have looked at Moses and said, “Not yet.”
He could have said, “I need more time.”
He could have stayed in the shadow where it felt familiar.
But God speaks through Moses in Deuteronomy 31:7–8, not with suggestion—but with command:
“Be strong and courageous… for the LORD your God goes with you. He will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Notice that.

God didn’t give Joshua a strategy first.
He gave him His presence.
Because the real battle was never about leadership.
It was about trust.
Here’s the AHA moment:
You don’t need to feel ready when God has already gone before you.
Read that again.
We think courage is the absence of fear.

But Scripture shows us something deeper—
courage is obedience in the presence of fear because you trust who goes before you.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

You say you trust God…
but you’re still waiting for a version of yourself that doesn’t need Him.
And that’s where the struggle gets real.

Because some of you are not just afraid of failure—
you’re afraid of stepping out without your old support system.

The mentor.
The relationship.
The environment that made you feel secure.

You’re standing in a season where something is ending…
but you’re still clinging to it while God is already speaking your next step.
Let me ask you:

What are you holding onto that God is already asking you to release?
What step have you been delaying because you don’t feel “ready enough”?
This is the moment.
Because here’s the deeper truth:

Joshua’s calling wasn’t about replacing Moses.
It was about walking with God for himself.

And some of you are trying to inherit someone else’s intimacy with God
instead of building your own.

You want their oil.
Their authority.
Their confidence.
But God is not cloning callings.
He is forming sons and daughters.
And this is where the Gospel breaks in.
Because the greatest fear behind all of this isn’t just inadequacy.
It’s separation.

It’s the quiet dread that when the season changes—
God might not be as close as He was before.
But listen—
Jesus didn’t just promise presence.
He secured it.

We were the ones who delayed.
We were the ones who doubted.
We were the ones who chose sin, chose comfort, chose self.
And Romans 3:23 reminds us plainly: all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.
That’s the real problem.

Not your lack of readiness.
Your separation from holiness.
But God didn’t leave it there.

John 3:16 doesn’t whisper—it declares:
“For God so loved the world that He gave His only Son…”

Jesus stepped into our failure.
Carried our sin to the cross.
Took the punishment we deserved.
And three days later—He rose.
Victory.

Not just over death—
but over everything that disqualifies you.
So now, through Christ, the promise in Deuteronomy 31 isn’t just historical—
It’s personal.

Hebrews 13:5 echoes it:
“I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Not because you’re strong.
But because Jesus already secured your place.
Here’s the conviction:
You can’t preach surrender and still negotiate obedience.
Here’s your identity:

You are not the one trying to prove you’re ready.
You are the one being called, covered, and carried by Christ.

You are not stepping into emptiness.
You are stepping into a path where God has already gone before you.
And maybe today is your Deuteronomy 31 moment.

Not clean.
Not comfortable.
Not fully understood.
But clear.
God is calling.
So what now?

Repent of the delay.
Release what you’ve been gripping.
Step forward—not because you feel strong…
…but because Jesus is.
If this pierced something in you, don’t ignore it.
Whisper this right now:
“OPEN MY HEART.”
Stay close.
Follow if you’re ready to grow—God is not done speaking.
And the next word might be the one that changes everything.
